title: Optimized Dynamical Decoupling for Spin Ensembles with Large Inhomogeneities
authors: Rajan Paul, Genko Genov, Oliver Schmid, Shinobu Onoda, Yutaka Kobayashi, Junichi Isoya, Fedor Jelezko
abstract: Spin ensembles show increasing promise for highly efficient quantum sensing and quantum technologies. However, protecting their coherent properties remains a significant challenge. Dynamical decoupling (DD) typically employs a sequence of fast pulses that aim to reduce the effect of unwanted system-environment interactions. However, the performance of the DD sequences typically suffers in spin ensembles, e.g., due to amplitude and frequency inhomogeneities and control errors. In this work, we compare the performance of an extensive number of DD protocols for coherence protection and quantum sensing in an ensemble of negatively charged NV centers under ambient conditions. We identify the optimal approach that uses rapid adiabatic passage pulses, which are robust to amplitude and frequency inhomogeneity, in combination with the variation of their phases. We experimentally demonstrate an improved signal contrast and an order-of-magnitude increase in memory time with the optimal sequence compared to the widely used XY8 with standard rectangular pulses. We also apply our approach for improved sensing of a weak oscillating field. While our particular demonstration is with NV centers in diamond, the optimized protocol is generally applicable to other spin ensembles and to systems with high amplitude and/or frequency inhomogeneities.
summary: This paper develops and experimentally validates optimized Dynamical Decoupling (DD) sequences for protecting quantum coherence in NV spin ensembles. By replacing standard square pulses with adiabatically shaped Rapid Adiabatic Passage (RAP) pulses, the researchers significantly extend the memory time and improve the signal contrast. This optimized protocol is shown to be generally applicable for high-inhomogeneity spin systems and is successfully applied for enhanced quantum sensing.
main_problem: Protecting the coherent properties of spin ensembles from environmental noise, especially when the system exhibits large amplitude and frequency inhomogeneities.
main_result: The optimal coherence protection protocol involves using Rapid Adiabatic Passage (RAP) pulses combined with phase variation, achieving an order-of-magnitude increase in memory time compared to standard sequences.
method: The authors compare numerous Dynamical Decoupling (DD) protocols, optimizing pulse shaping by replacing standard rectangular pulses with smooth, adiabatic pulse envelopes.
model_or_system: The study uses negatively charged Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers in diamond as the spin ensemble platform. The dynamics are modeled using the von Neumann equation, focusing on the evolution of the Bloch vector.
key_observables: Coherence time ($T_2$), signal contrast, and the ability to sense weak oscillating magnetic fields (AC magnetometry).
important_parameters: Amplitude and frequency inhomogeneities ($\epsilon, \delta_\epsilon$), pulse duration ($T_{	ext{pulse}}$), and the Rabi frequency ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The primary limitation addressed is the presence of significant and varying environmental noise ($\delta_\epsilon$ and $\epsilon$) in the spin ensemble.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy level diagrams, experimental setups, and crucial comparisons of Rabi oscillations decay curves showing the superior contrast and longer coherence times achieved with RAP pulses versus standard pulses.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares various DD protocols, introduces the concept of pulse shaping (sine/parabolic envelopes), demonstrates the robustness of RAP pulses against inhomogeneities, and finally applies the optimized sequence to measure external magnetic fields.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, experimentally validated techniques (RAP pulse shaping) to push the limits of coherence in solid-state quantum memories, which is crucial for building practical quantum sensors and quantum information processors.
